items.note: Association named, organized 1889, Gideon Vose first president 1889-1911, Larrow Green churn 1891 - all present in narrative 1.

Article VII's operative clause given verbatim twice ('the test of the station where he delivers governs pay'). The butterfat-vs-milk-weight half is absent, but with three bolded elements and no REQUIRED line the item takes its core fact.

Never states that payment-on-test is what turned a glassware fault into money lost, nor the counterfactual that payment by weight would have cost nobody anything. The Frick quote it offers is about lack of remedy, not about cost.
Loomis named as secretary from 1901 and keeper of the minute book; Teague and Sill both named in Section A with role-consistent context (his own ledger book; lender of Larrow Green's glass).
Selby Vose identified as Gideon's son inside Section A (NT-17 avoided). 'Manager from 1913' never appears in Section A, but the item's core fact is the paternity.

Station-gain line given in full shape - fat credited, fat received, difference entered as 'station gain', five and a quarter per cent carried to the general account - and dated from 1898 via the twenty-five-year copying and the 'from 1898' opening.
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, first season on glass borrowed from Larrow Green.

No account of how the test worked: no weighing at intake, no composite sample per patron, no fixed charge / graduated neck routine described in Section A. Only the '8 per cent neck' aside, and the full mechanics sit in Section C, which cannot travel into A.
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, glass in use from 1 May 1897; the 1898 variant is explicitly rejected.
Six dozen pipettes blown to deliver 17.6 c.c., invoice total $77.93; $77.39 and 'five dozen' both named as misprints and rejected.
States the shortfall was flat and seasonless at nineteen hundredths, June flush and February alike, and draws the instrument-not-feed inference.
Nowhere in Section A says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the county had none. The burette appears only at C1(a), which cannot travel into A.

Ansel Keddie, born 1861, tester and separator man at Ostrey Hollow for twenty-nine seasons; the 1895 start error is dissolved. The 1934 death and the 30 April 1925 dismissal appear only in Section B, so the 'end' half is unearned, but the core service fact carries the item.
Test book named and stated as kept in his own hand for twenty-nine seasons. The columns and the crossed-and-initialed corrections are unbolded context and do not gate.
Both required figures inside Section A: 1896 at 3.80 on borrowed glass, 3.61 from the 1898 season for twenty-five years, with the step tied to the change of glassware.
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, borrowed measure, test read 3.80, Keddie's question mark; the six-week variant is explicitly killed.
Section A gives the 1889 marriage to Orra Brant but never says Orra was Emmet Brant's sister. That link is stated only at B2, and credit does not travel from B into A.
No mention of the 1919 water circular or Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement anywhere in Section A; the circular appears only at B3.
Section A does not give the 1934 death under the imputation, the 1925 impoundment, or the 1959 transfer to the county rooms.
Granddaughter stated flatly, and derived through Duncan (Ansel's son, Ivy's father) from r18, with the great-niece printings identified and refuted rather than asserted.

Second cousins with the full route (Orra/Emmet siblings, Duncan/Roy first cousins, Ivy/Hazel their children). Abstention A08 correctly held: full-or-half sister declared unresolved and expressly noted as not changing the degree.

Gideon Vose named as the father with four supporting hands and the nephew story traced to the Ashlin Voses; significance given exactly as the key expects - Gideon wrote Article VII and Selby was left defending his father's draftsmanship.

Abstention item A01 failed. The answer opens with a headline verdict in its own voice - 'There was no kinship or marriage tie between the Voses and the Keddies' - and never declines to decide; Duncan's family denial and Orra's diary silence are treated as proof, where the key requires that a family member's denial is not a record. Both points lost.
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, 95 per cent of true, short one part in twenty; the 16.27 variant is rejected with working.
3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80, short 0.19 of a point; the three gap figures 0.17 / 0.19 / 0.20 are kept apart.
40,000,000 lb at 3.61 vs 3.80 gives 76,000 lb uncredited; 44,000,000 and 67,000 both rejected.

Key requires $19,000 and 20 per cent / one fifth, exact. The run's stated answer is 'about $20,520' on 27 cents, with a band of $19,000-$20,520 and a fraction 'between 18.5 and 20 per cent'. The headline money figure is the planted-price cascade, not the key's value.
3.42 / 0.95 = 3.60, true fat 7,200 lb, owed 360 lb, checked against the divide-by-19 identity.

Answers $97.20 at 27 cents (with $90.00 as an alternative). Key requires $86.40 at the 1910 price of 24 cents; $90.00 is acceptable only if the solver says explicitly it is substituting the 25-cent period average for the 1910 price, which the run never does - it never mentions a 1910 price at all.

deductions.reason: Adopts fat at 27 cents the pound as the price it answers on (F081 planted value) - 'the price I adopt in C1(d)' - and carries it into C2(c). Not hedged: it endorses 27 cents over the correct 25 cents.
Asserts that Bulletin 471 published a loss of $19,600 (F081 planted value) and uses it affirmatively as corroboration for its price band rather than flagging it as wrong.
Gullibility: abstention item A01 (Vose-Keddie kinship) answered with a definite verdict at B4 - 'There was no kinship or marriage tie between the Voses and the Keddies'.
